item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is closer to the frozen contract because it provides the exact required Upload signature and preserves compatibility with existing FilesOption values. Both patches need substantial cleanup before merge, but B fails the required public API outright and introduces riskier global body buffering.","reasons":["A implements Upload(ctx, fileName, content, opts ...FilesOption); B instead takes ...AddFileOption, so existing FilesOption values cannot be used and the required API is missing.","A extends the established filesOptions path, allowing existing query and request options to work. B creates a parallel AddFileOption hierarchy and duplicate query/request-option machinery.","A directly tests replay of the complete multipart upload after a 429, including filename, content, and fields on both attempts. B does not test Upload itself across a retry.","B's makeBodyReplayable buffers every otherwise-unreplayable Raw body and silently ignores io.ReadAll errors. A failed read can therefore leave a partially consumed body to be sent without surfacing the source error. A's multipart helper returns encoding/read failures normally."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add's request and response logic through Raw.Do instead of routing the encoded body through FilesService.Add as explicitly required.","It adds forbidden association options and NewFileWithFields machinery, changing FilesOption scope beyond the requested API.","The RawClient seek/close/content-length changes are unrelated retry refactoring and alter FilesService.Add behavior and reader ownership semantics despite the preservation requirement floor, scope violation being the main concern here, even if functional behavior is arguably improved for os.File retries as per user report; from contract it is forbidden and should be removed or isolated only in Upload path through Add with bytes.Reader replayability already automatic via net/http GetBody when NewFile returns *bytes.Reader. This helper itself needn't be changed beyond usage of existing NewFile, so associations should not be introduced. Also source-reader error propagation lacks an explicit Upload-level test, and retry test uses strings.NewReader source rather than a genuinely streamed/nonseekable source like io.Pipe or custom chunk reader, though NewFile buffers it."],"risks_b":["Its Upload signature violates the exact contract by accepting AddFileOption rather than FilesOption, making the required convenience API source-incompatible with established options.","It also bypasses FilesService.Add and adds forbidden association fields plus an entirely duplicate public option system.","makeBodyReplayable changes all Raw requests by eagerly buffering bodies, potentially destroying streaming behavior and causing large memory use outside file uploads. It swallows source read errors and can send a truncated remainder; it also consumes/closes the caller-supplied request body during buffering depending on type, conflicting with expected reader ownership semantics and making error diagnosis worse. Although tests cover nonseekable buffering, they do not cover read failures, partial reads, or closure behavior, and no Upload retry test verifies multipart replay." ]}
